original_question: Can one find a way to evaluate the Kodaira dimension kappa(M) of the moduli space M without necessarily analyzing the singularities of M directly?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.2 in Section 2, “Problems to be solved in the future – Singularities and Kodaira dimension,” with the immediately following sentence sharpening the intended scope to the case κ(X)=1 and c1=0.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact core of the paper’s open problem: it asks for a way to determine the Kodaira dimension κ(M) while avoiding a direct analysis of the singularities of M. It also correctly keeps the focus on κ(M), rather than drifting to broader birational questions.
missing_details: M is not an arbitrary moduli space: in the paper it is the coarse moduli scheme M = M_H(v) of rank-two H-stable sheaves with fixed Chern classes v = (2, c1, c2) on a complex projective smooth surface X over C (Section 1, Problem 1.1, p. 13).

In the specific setting continued into Section 2, the standing assumptions are that κ(X)=1 and c1=0; earlier in Section 1 this is the case where X is assumed to be a minimal surface, hence an elliptic surface (Section 1, p. 13; Section 2, p. 15).

To stay fully faithful to the nearby notation, one should identify the main moduli space in this setting as M_H((2,0,c2)) = M(c2) = M, and H is assumed to be v-suitable for the chosen Chern data (Section 1, pp. 13-14).

The problem is about determining the actual Kodaira dimension κ(M), not merely producing partial birational information, lower bounds, or proving that M is of general type in some unrelated regime (Problem 2.2, p. 15).

The motivation being bypassed should be stated: in the surrounding discussion, κ(M) is obtained by first proving the singularities are canonical and then using the comparison between Friedman’s map and the pluricanonical map; Problem 2.2 asks whether one can avoid that singularity-first route (Theorem 1.2 and Proposition 1.3, p. 14; Theorem 1.6 and Theorem 1.7, p. 15).

The paper immediately narrows the hoped-for application of Problem 2.2 to the above-mentioned case κ(X)=1 and c1=0, so a stand-alone version should include that specialization explicitly (sentence after Problem 2.2, p. 16).

No hidden conditions about homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, operators, or 'for all sufficiently large m' belong to this problem; the relevant ambient data are geometric: X over C, H, the fixed rank-two Chern data, and the moduli scheme M.
refined_question: Let X be a complex projective smooth minimal surface with κ(X)=1, let v=(2,0,c2), and let H be a v-suitable ample line bundle on X. If M=M_H(v) denotes the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves on X with Chern classes v, can one determine the Kodaira dimension κ(M) by a method that avoids directly confronting the singularities of M, in particular without first having to decide whether those singularities are canonical?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s official open problem, namely Problem 2.2 in Section 2 (p. 15). What it omits is the definition of M from Section 1 and the paper’s standing specialization to the κ(X)=1, c1=0 minimal elliptic-surface setting (Problem 1.1, p. 13; Section 2, p. 15). The nearby context shows why singularities are the issue: Friedman’s map is compared with the pluricanonical map in Theorem 1.2 and Proposition 1.3 (p. 14), and in the favorable case Theorem 1.6 computes κ(M) by first proving canonical singularities, while Theorem 1.7 explains why second-order singularity analysis can fail (p. 15). The sentence immediately after Problem 2.2 then explicitly asks for such an approach in the above-mentioned case κ(X)=1 and c1=0 (p. 16).
